title: Rising Seas
objective: After this level you can explain why sea level is rising.
summary: Seas have risen about 21 to 24 cm since 1880 as warming water expands and land ice melts. The rise is speeding up, and the IPCC expects more.

cards.headline: Global sea level has risen about 21–24 cm since 1880.
cards.body: That's a bit more than the length of a new pencil, added to every coastline on Earth. And the rise is speeding up. So where is all that extra water coming from?

cards.headline: Two taps are running
cards.body: Sea level rises for two main reasons. First, seawater expands as it warms, and Level 36 showed the ocean has taken up about 91% of the extra heat. Second, glaciers and ice sheets on land are melting and adding water. From 1971 to 2018, the IPCC found expansion caused about 50% of the rise, glaciers about 22% and ice sheets about 20%. Same ocean, just puffed up and topped up.

cards.headline: Not a trickle any more
cards.body: The rise isn't steady. The IPCC measured about 1.3 mm a year from 1901 to 1971, and about 3.7 mm a year from 2006 to 2018: nearly three times as fast. Human influence was very likely the main driver since at least 1971. A millimeter sounds tiny, but a tap that keeps speeding up eventually fills the bath.

cards.headline: What the IPCC expects
cards.body: It depends on us. By 2100, the IPCC's likely rise is 0.28–0.55 m with very low emissions and 0.63–1.01 m with very high emissions, compared with 1995–2014. Rises approaching 2 m can't be ruled out, because ice-sheet behavior is deeply uncertain, and sea level is committed to keep rising for centuries.

mascot.line: Notice the ranges. The future sea isn't one number, and the choices people make move it.

cards.headline: Rising seas: measured
learned: Warming water expands; land ice melts
IPCC 2100: likely 0.28–0.55 m to 0.63–1.01 m, by emissions

questions.prompt: What are the two main reasons global sea level is rising?

options.label: Warm water expands and land ice melts
More rain falls and rivers get bigger
options.rationale: Rain and rivers just move water around.

options.label: Sea ice freezes and undersea volcanoes erupt
Tides get stronger and waves get bigger
options.rationale: Tides and waves don't raise average sea level.

questions.explanation: Seawater expands as it warms, and melting glaciers and ice sheets add water to the ocean.

questions.prompt: The IPCC found about 1.3 mm a year of rise in 1901 to 1971 and about 3.7 mm a year in 2006 to 2018. What does that show?

options.label: The rise stopped after 1971
options.rationale: The later rate is higher, not zero.

options.label: The measurements must be wrong
options.rationale: Both come from the IPCC's assessment.

questions.explanation: The rate nearly tripled, so the rise is accelerating; human influence was very likely the main driver since at least 1971.

questions.prompt: Level 36: the ocean has taken up about 91% of the extra heat. How does that heat raise the sea?

options.label: It evaporates the sea, which then rains back more
It makes the sea floor sink
options.rationale: The sea floor isn't the cause.

options.label: It doesn't: only melting ice matters
options.rationale: Expansion caused about half the rise from 1971 to 2018.

options.label: Warmer seawater expands and takes up more room

questions.explanation: Warm water expands. From 1971 to 2018 that expansion caused about half of global sea-level rise.
